findings.finding: No SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers are installed. The imported native module defines handlers only inside its uncalled main. Default SIGTERM/HUP can exit this guard without entering its cleanup path while the separately sessioned child remains active.
findings.minimal_fix: Install signal.SIGTERM and signal.SIGHUP handlers that raise InterruptedError before entering the protected lifecycle. Keep existing BaseException cleanup/own-group-only signaling. No signal to a host-inventory PID.

findings.finding: Program/source pins are checked before a potentially unbounded host wait. They are not rechecked just before Popen; generic check_probe has no live HEAD check. The post-command tool hash catches a change only after the changed program has already executed, and HEAD/clean state is not rechecked afterward.
findings.minimal_fix: After wait_idle/resources and immediately before Popen, repeat allowed tool/native-helper hashes and live HEAD/clean checks. Repeat HEAD/clean after the child together with existing tool hashes. Preserve raw command rc separately from guard failure.

positive_findings: Pinned import does not launch the native runner main and disables bytecode writes.
Nested allowed final-driver/checker subprocess calls inherit the newly sessioned guard child PGID; no nested start_new_session/preexec_fn was found.
Collision path calls only stop_own_group on the just-created child, never a PID from host inventory.
Actual command status is returned; expected native rc1 is not converted into success, and outcome_interpreted stays false.
Ordinary PATH and no PFR configuration are used.
limits: No import/execution of the guard, native helper, checker, final runner or probe.
No signal/process simulation, native/cache/app operation or source/Git mutation.
This is a host-guard review; source/Name/seal outcomes remain the underlying driver and final-evidence review responsibility.
